The CSV export in reports/export.py crashes on rows that contain a comma inside a quoted field. Fix it and add a test.
I'll look at the exporter first.

The exporter joins fields with commas by hand and the parser splits on every comma, so a quoted field with a comma breaks both. The standard library's csv module handles quoting correctly; I'll switch both functions to it.
Now a regression test with commas, quotes and newlines inside fields.

arguments.content:
from reports.export import export_rows, parse_rows


def test_round_trip_with_commas_and_quotes():
    rows = [
        {'name': 'Smith, John', 'note': 'said "hi"', 'qty': 3},
        {'name': 'Ada', 'note': 'line one\nline two', 'qty': 12},
    ]
    text = export_rows(rows, ['name', 'note', 'qty'])
    back = parse_rows(text)
    assert [r['name'] for r in back] == ['Smith, John', 'Ada']
    assert back[0]['note'] == 'said "hi"'
    assert back[1]['note'] == 'line one\nline two'
    assert back[1]['qty'] == '12'


def test_header_only():
    assert parse_rows(export_rows([], ['a', 'b'])) == []

messages.content: Fixed. `reports/export.py` now uses `csv.DictWriter` and `csv.DictReader`, which quote fields that contain commas, quotes or newlines and read them back intact. Values come back as strings, as before. I added `tests/test_export.py` with a round trip over a comma, embedded quotes and a multi-line field, plus an empty export; both tests pass.
Thanks. Large reports run out of memory now that everything is built in one string. Can export_rows write straight to a file?
Yes. I'll add a `dest` argument: any text file object (or a path) receives the rows as they are written, and without it the function keeps returning a string so existing callers work unchanged.

The function now returns `out.getvalue()` only when it created the buffer itself; with a file it streams each row and returns None. Rows are consumed one at a time, so a generator of rows never sits in memory as a whole. I also added `import os` at the top. Run `python -m pytest -q` to check the existing tests still pass, and pass `dest='report.csv'` for the large exports.
